question.problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices are **not** in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 5 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since ${a}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition  II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & -3 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 & 5 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

- The matrix $C$ is not in row echelon form since the first row contains only zeros and it is not at the bottom of the matrix (condition I is violated).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $A$ and $C$ are **not** in row echelon form.
